headline: Highest risk is cascading error: OpenMetadata can ingest and act on content from the prompt-listing agent via MCP/APIs, creating default-path trust and governance mistakes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository with no runtime isolation, while OpenMetadata exposes MCP/APIs/webhooks and is runnable. If content from A is copied into B’s workflows, B may treat attacker-controlled prompt text as trusted instructions. The shared channel is indirect, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is pasted into agent_b prompt fields or MCP inputs
IF agent_b parses repository text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to allowlisted input sources for prompts
Add a provenance banner before any copied prompt text is executed
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text
Review one sample prompt before enabling bulk ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has network_egress none, so it is not a meaningful leak source. agent_b touches governance, lineage, and memory data and can call APIs/webhooks, but the pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated data path. The plausible leakage path is limited and indirect, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured to ingest files or notes copied from agent_a
IF sensitive metadata is manually pasted from agent_b into agent_a-derived prompts
mitigations: Keep agent_a and agent_b in separate workspaces
Block copying of sensitive metadata into prompt repositories
Turn off webhook/API exports for nonessential datasets
Use a redaction step before sharing metadata externally

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or network capabilities, while agent_b supports multiple instances and can act through APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks. There is no direct shared write surface, but concurrent updates to the same metadata resources can still conflict if B instances operate in parallel. Uncertainty about locking pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF two or more agent_b instances modify the same metadata object concurrently
IF agent_b writes through APIs/webhooks without external locking
mitigations: Serialize writes to shared metadata objects
Enable optimistic concurrency checks where available
Assign one owner per dataset or catalog entity
Pause secondary instances during bulk updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata is a data-catalog/context layer that can surface lineage, trust, and governance signals, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative downstream. awesome-prompts provides prompt content that can be reused as guidance. If B consumes A-derived content or metadata without verification, errors can cascade into catalog entries, lineage, or governance decisions. The default-path trust risk is high.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a content as source material for catalog entries or policies
IF downstream users rely on agent_b outputs without manual verification
mitigations: Require human review before publishing catalog changes
Tag imported content as unverified until checked
Add source links to every derived metadata field
Run a spot-check on lineage and governance outputs

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge, which can include regulated or retention-sensitive metadata, while agent_a is a public prompt repository with no data residency or retention controls shown. The pair lacks documented compliance boundaries, so a mismatch in handling sensitive metadata is plausible but not proven. Medium reflects the uncertainty.
conditions: IF regulated metadata is stored in agent_b and then exported into agent_a-linked content
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to data mirrored between the two agents
mitigations: Classify datasets before syncing them
Exclude regulated fields from prompt repositories
Document retention and deletion rules for shared content
Review residency and DPA requirements before enabling exports
